content: What is the diameter of the round window in ZETA?

No data: no structure named ['round window']. Available: Bone, Carotis Interna, Chorda Tympani, Cochleovestibular nerve, External Auditory Canal, Facial Nerve, Incus, Malleus, Scala Tympani, Scala Vestibuli, Sinus Dura, Stapes, Tympanic Membrane.

CochleaHub doesn't have a round window diameter for ZETA. The round window isn't a segmented structure in the dataset. The structures available are Bone, Carotis Interna, Chorda Tympani, Cochleovestibular nerve, External Auditory Canal, Facial Nerve, Incus, Malleus, Scala Tympani, Scala Vestibuli, Sinus Dura, Stapes and Tympanic Membrane.

The closest measurement is cochlear dimension A, but it isn't the same thing. In clinical practice, A is the basal-turn diameter (round window to the opposite wall). That is the cochlear basal-turn diameter, not the diameter of the round window opening.

CochleaHub also doesn't measure A with the round window as a landmark. A/B/height are a landmark-free proxy. The classical definitions use the round window and modiolar axis; landmark detection as in [Stebani2023] is future work. The proxy is the oriented bounding box of the scala tympani.

I can pull ZETA's proxy A, B and height values, with their published reference ranges, if that would help.
